newsitem.title: USA: Shoe Carnival Jan. same-store sales off.
newsitem.headline: Shoe Carnival Jan. same-store sales off.

text.p: Shoe Carnival Inc said Thursday that January same-store sales declined 1.7 percent when compared to the same 1996 period.
Total sales for the four weeks ended February 1, 1997 decreased 21.5 percent to $11.6 million from $14.8 million for the five-week period ended February 3, 1996.

Shoe Carnival also posted sales results for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996 and the 1996 fiscal year, all periods which ended on February 1, 1997 and consisted of four weeks, 13 weeks and fifty-two weeks, respectively. The same periods in the prior year consisted of five weeks, 14 weeks and 53 weeks, respectively.

Total sales for the 13-week fourth quarter of fiscal 1996 fell 5.8 percent to $54.2 million from sales of $57.6 million in the 14-week period ended February 3, 1996. Comparable store sales for comparable 13-week periods increased 0.6 percent.

Sales for the 1996 fiscal year ended February 1, 1997 increased 2.5 percent to $233.9 million from sales of $228.3 million in the 53 week period ended February 3, 1996. Comparable store sales decreased 1.1 percent for the comparable 52 week periods.

"The decrease in sales for the fiscal month of January, as compared to the fiscal month of January 1996, resulted from the inclusion of the additional week of sales in January 1996," said president Mark Lemond in a statement.

"Although extreme weather conditions in the Midwest hindered sales in the middle of the month, we recorded very strong sales results during the more normal weather patterns of the final week," Lemond continued. "Gross profit margins in January were significantly higher than last year, continuing the trend we saw in December. This is a reflection of a much improved inventory position relative to last year, in terms of both quality and quantity."
